category_title: Elementary students with severe behavioral disorders exhibiting high-risk aggressive and disruptive behaviors
minimal_context: The student is participating in a 10-minute teacher-led math lesson on number properties while seated at their desk.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's look at the whiteboard for our math lesson on number properties. Please sit quietly and look at the examples.

STUDENT: (Twists body away from the location of the learning stimuli on the white board for more than 5 seconds) I'm not looking at that. (Starts talking to the student at the next desk)

TUTOR: You need to focus on your own assignment.

STUDENT: (Continues speaking to others while the teacher talks) Make me! (Forcefully pushes the student next to him)

TUTOR: Stop that right now and get back to work.

STUDENT: (Stands up, leaving the desk so no body part touches the chair for more than 5 seconds) I'm done with this! (Shouts, raising voice beyond an average volume practiced in the class)

options.A: Give the student a simplified task on number properties while the rest of the class completes the standard lesson.
options.B: Prompt the student to use manipulatives to represent the number properties, linking them to a math sentence on the whiteboard.
options.C: Provide an explicit explanation of the number properties and assign specific roles for manipulating the examples during the lesson.
options.D: Use instructional antecedents such as interactive teaching, eye contact, and appropriate physical proximity during the whiteboard lesson.
